solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lives with husband born in Turkey, perhaps where there's no privacy

indicators.note: in places the lives-husband-born group inside the bird

parts.note: a turkey is an example of fowl, which the 'perhaps' signals
lives means is, as in 'exists'
B is the abbreviation for born, as in family records

explanation.surface: A married couple living and having a baby in Turkey, perhaps with nosy neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: Turkey with its capital looks like the country, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A goldfish bowl is an idiom for a setting where everything you do is watched from all sides.

clue.text: Boundless packaging started with fine slushy drink

indicators.note: started with puts the fine letter at the front

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, on pencils

indicators.note: boundless strips the outside letters from the packaging word

parts.note: a wrapper is packaging

explanation.surface: Endless packaging around a fine iced drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boundless' drops both ends of WRAPPER, leaving RAPPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A frappé is a drink served with crushed ice, hence slushy.

clue.text: Informant primarily involved in break-up of a rash legal system

indicators.note: involved in places the initial letter inside the jumbled letters
break-up of says the letters of a rash are broken apart and reset
primarily takes just the leading letter of Informant

explanation.surface: An informer is caught up in a break-up of a hasty legal process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break-up of' makes SHARA from A RASH; 'involved in' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharia is Islamic law, a code of rules derived from the Koran.

clue.text: Standard heath rises, choked by live parasitic plant

indicators.note: choked by means the live word grips the rest inside

parts.note: to be is to live, exist

indicators.note: rises in a down clue says the pieces read from bottom up

parts.note: par is a standard, as in golf
a moor is open heathland

explanation.surface: A standard heathland plant grows, but a living parasite chokes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns PARMOOR into ROOMRAP, held by BE.
explanation.definitionFit: Broomrape is a leafless plant that feeds on the roots of other plants, a parasite by nature.

clue.text: With the man's waistband raised, see fly's irregular exposure

parts.note: his means belonging to the man

indicators.note: raised in a down clue says the belt word reads upwards

parts.note: a belt goes round the waist
lo means look or see, as in lo and behold
a wing belongs to a fly

explanation.surface: A man hitches up his trousers to reveal his fly undone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' gives TLEB from BELT; the surface suggests indecent exposure, but this exposure is of wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Revealing an organisation's misconduct outside normal channels is the irregular disclosure meant.

clue.text: Group keeping most of company away from scrutiny

indicators.note: keeping means the group holds the shortened company inside it

parts.note: a set is a group

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter of the company word

parts.note: a crew is a company of people working together

explanation.surface: A club keeps most of its business hidden from public view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'company' suggests a firm, but here it is a crew of workers or sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept private, unseen by the inquisitive, is a synonym-level match for hidden from inspection.

clue.text: Keeping head down, conceals immoral actions

indicators.note: head down shifts the leading letter one place lower in the down entry

parts.note: veils means covers or hides

explanation.surface: Someone lying low hides bad deeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping head down' moves V of VEILS down one place.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked deeds are wrongs, a plain synonym for sins.

clue.text: Assign new lines to escape rent in radio-telephony

indicators.note: in places the pair of pieces inside the radio letters

parts.note: RT is the abbreviation for radio-telephony
Esc is the escape key on a keyboard
a rip is a rent or tear

explanation.surface: Rewriting scripts to avoid paying rent, over the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: To rewrite a script means to give actors new dialogue, a verb formed from re- plus script.

clue.text: Stink in US accepted by second person once ex-president was named thus

indicators.note: accepted by means the archaic pronoun takes the smell inside

parts.note: thee is the old form of you
odor is the American spelling of a smell

explanation.surface: A former US president was named after a bad smell.
explanation.walkthrough: Theodore Roosevelt was a US president.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore Roosevelt, the 26th president, carried this forename.

clue.text: Inflammatory item from civil engineer in local journal bundle?

indicators.note: in places the engineer letters inside the pub

parts.note: a local is a British pub, here an inn
a diary is a journal
a bundle is a large sum of money, as is a bomb in British slang

explanation.surface: A provocative story from an engineer in a parish newspaper bundle.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is a neighbourhood pub; 'cost a bomb' and 'make a bundle' both mean lots of money in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: A firebomb is an explosive designed to start fires, literally setting things alight.

clue.text: Internet giant (giant without borders) associated with large-scale streaming

parts.note: Amazon is the huge online retailer

indicators.note: without borders strips the outside letters from the second giant

explanation.surface: A tech firm is linked with big video streaming services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without borders' leaves IAN from GIANT. The 'streaming' is not video but the Amazon river, the world's largest by flow.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything belonging to the Amazon, the river with the greatest water flow on Earth.

clue.text: One shouldn't initially prosecute publication

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the word shouldn't

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action, i.e. prosecute

explanation.surface: Advice that a person should not take a newspaper to court.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition of a magazine or newspaper is called an issue, a noun for something published.

clue.text: Politician protecting gentleman over something that colours views?

indicators.note: protecting means the politician surrounds the other piece

parts.note: PM is Prime Minister, a politician

indicators.note: over signals turning the gentleman's title around

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight or gentleman

explanation.surface: A politician guarding a nobleman, perhaps biased in outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' signals the turnaround of the title; PM is Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass prism splits white light into a rainbow, literally adding colour to what is seen through it; the question mark flags the wit.

clue.text: Certainly breaking step that is thought highly of

indicators.note: breaking means one word bursts into the middle of the other

parts.note: a tread is a step, as on a staircase
sure means certainly, as in a reply

explanation.surface: Confidently interrupting a dance step that is greatly admired.
explanation.definitionFit: Something treasured is valued and cherished, which is a synonym of being highly regarded.

clue.text: He may hear private confessions, new Pope's averred

indicators.note: new says the following words are made anew in fresh order

parts.note: the 's here stands for 'is' contracted, so its S is part of the letters

explanation.surface: A new Pope claims he will hear private confessions.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a priest in the confessional; the definition is anyone listening in secretly.
explanation.definitionFit: A snooper secretly listens to private conversations, so might catch confessions not meant for them.

clue.text: Old special constable having a third go, embarrassed to change sides

parts.note: SC is a special constable, a volunteer police officer

indicators.note: having a third go loses the final third of the embarrassed phrase

parts.note: ill at ease means uncomfortable or embarrassed

explanation.surface: A volunteer policeman on his third attempt is too embarrassed to defect.
explanation.walkthrough: ILL AT EASE has nine letters; losing the last three leaves ILLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To swing back and forth is to move repeatedly from one side to the other.

clue.text: Inland Revenue catching several in charge with elements in another arrangement

indicators.note: catching means the revenue letters hold the other word inside

parts.note: IR is the old UK tax authority
some means several
IC is in charge

explanation.surface: Tax officials catching several people in charge of differently arranged items.
explanation.definitionFit: Isomers are compounds with the same atoms in a different structure, so the adjective fits.

clue.text: Online provocateur, endlessly forthright writer

parts.note: a troll provokes others online

indicators.note: endlessly drops the last letter of the forthright word

parts.note: open means frank or forthright

explanation.surface: An internet troll, endlessly outspoken, writes away.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Trollope was a Victorian English novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope, author of the Barsetshire novels, is an example of a novelist.

clue.text: What's done by "cruel, evil," NSA?

indicators.note: done in the sense of done over, beaten up, so the letters of the quoted words are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the US National Security Agency, taken as letters

explanation.surface: A question about what a supposedly cruel and evil spy agency does.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the agency's notorious activity is spying.
explanation.definitionFit: The NSA is famous for close monitoring and spying on communications, which is what this activity is.

clue.text: Accuse an element of vindictiveness

indicators.note: an element of says the letters are a component inside vindictiveness

explanation.surface: Accusing someone has a touch of spite to it.
explanation.definitionFit: To formally charge with a crime is to accuse, a legal synonym.

clue.text: Sport brings in one million for German city

indicators.note: brings in means the sport word takes the pair inside

parts.note: to sport clothes is to wear them
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A sports team earns a million for a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Weimar is a city in Thuringia, Germany, known for Goethe and the Weimar Republic.

clue.text: Vacant part of Libya was eliminated in revolution

indicators.note: in revolution says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A report that part of Libya was knocked out of a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Vacant part' as the definition, but 'part of' signals the hidden letters; 'Vacant' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone daydreaming is said to be distant in thought, an idiom for a blank, absent expression.

clue.text: Former security force curtailed equilibrium

indicators.note: curtailed cuts the tail off, dropping the final letter

parts.note: stasis is a state of balance

explanation.surface: An old security force cut short a balance of power.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stasi was the East German secret police, a former state security service.

clue.text: After breathing space, English foil attack?

indicators.note: after places the English letter following the breathing organ

parts.note: a lung is a space in the body for breathing

explanation.surface: After a pause for breath, an English fencer attacks with the foil.
explanation.definitionFit: In fencing, a thrust forward with the foil is a sudden forward attack, the move named here.

clue.text: Heard it from Navajo nomad? Almost conclusively it comes from grapevine

indicators.note: conclusively points to the closing letter of each word, and almost means one short of that, the second-to-last letter

parts.note: the word with its final letter set aside
the word with its final letter set aside
the word with its final letter set aside
the word with its final letter set aside
the word with its final letter set aside

explanation.surface: Gossip picked up from a wandering Navajo, about a rumour on the grapevine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard it on the grapevine' suggests gossip; here the grapevine is literal, as this is a wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a Spanish red wine, made from grapes grown on vines.

clue.text: Return of fascist groups means Zion must adapt

indicators.note: must adapt says these letters have to be rearranged

explanation.surface: As fascist groups revive, the Jewish homeland must respond.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix neo- means new or revived, so a revival of Hitler's ideology is exactly this.

clue.text: Trust councillor to prepare for broadcast

parts.note: to edit material is to get it ready to go on air

explanation.surface: Relying on a local politician to get material ready for airing.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit as a noun means belief or confidence, as in giving credit to a story.

clue.text: Dissident soldiers behind old boy caught aboard plane

indicators.note: behind puts the soldiers after the rest

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: aboard puts the caught letter inside the aircraft

parts.note: a jet is a plane
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A rebel soldier trails a former pupil captured on an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: OR means 'other ranks', soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissenter who refuses to conform is one who protests, a near synonym.
